title: docs(readme): Adding animated demo on the readme
body:
I've added an animated gif of what exactly is a full page "instant search". An image is worth a thousand words, so I feel it will be more compelling.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/283419/15489476/f6f07eae-2114-11e6-8d02-e1d66da173db.png)

comments.body: By analyzing the blame information on this pull request, we identified @vvo, @redox and @Jerskouille to be potential reviewers

It's a bit confusing to have it next to the website link.
Maybe it just needs a title.

> It's a bit confusing to have it next to the website link.
> Maybe it just needs a title.

What about putting it below the **Quick Start** section?

I've added a title but I'd really like to keep it at the top of the readme, so people can see and understand what it does really quickly.

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/283419/15523298/4b47b27e-21ce-11e6-8b7a-eaa2fcdbf784.png)

Why not show a demo of the examples part of the website (like the furnitures one) and link to that example page. We are currently showing an interface the user will not find anywhere on the instantsearch.js website.

Also add a small text like: "Here's an example of what can be built easily using instantsearch.js and Algolia:" then after the image "Find this example on our website at http://...examples/..." so that we are transparent on where we are linking.

Good point. I wanted to use the examples of the website at first, but I was struggling with doing an animated gif with nice enough colors (not dithered), and then I realized there is this gif we already use in several tutorials and slides we show at events. So I reused the same to stay consistent.

So instead of using an animated gif from the example page, why don't we add this example to the `/examples` page. We even have the full guide available on [instant search](https://www.algolia.com/doc/search/instant-search) demo. 

That's another point, but I would also like to add more external examples/demo to that page like [marvel](http://pixelastic.github.io/marvel/), [steamdb](https://steamdb.info/instantsearch/) or [searchstone](http://searchstone.io/).

And I've added some context as per your suggestion:

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/283419/15558304/d581cadc-228d-11e6-84e4-bb20e843038e.png)
